title: feat: initial Amp Code harness integration (toolpath-amp, preview)
body:
## What this adds

`toolpath-amp` 0.1.0, a both-directions **preview** provider for Amp (ampcode.com) threads, wired into the CLI end to end: forward (`path p import / list / show amp`, `path share`) and reverse via a new `AmpProjector` (`path p export amp`, `path resume --harness amp`). `path-cli` goes 0.16.0 to 0.17.0. `toolpath-cursor` picks up a real fix at 0.2.1 (details below).

## The two findings that shaped the design

**Amp threads are server-authoritative.** The per-thread log under `~/.cache/amp/logs/` is content-free telemetry and no other local file holds thread content, so the canonical artifact is the first-party `amp threads export <id>` document, fetched behind an injectable `ThreadFetcher` (`CliFetcher` live, `DirFetcher` offline; `cargo test` never touches the network or spends money).

**There is no import path for a document**, so resume is **context transfer, not transcript injection**: `amp threads new` (server-assigned id, never touches existing threads) plus `amp threads continue <id> -x` with a rendered transcript on stdin. The tempting REST-looking `POST /import` answers `201 Created` and creates nothing. This was disproven by read-back, with verbatim errors recorded in `docs/agents/formats/amp/writing-compatible.md`. The full-fidelity projection is filed INSERT-only at `~/.toolpath/amp-projected/<live-thread-id>.json`.

Token accounting follows the kind v1.1.0 clean per-message pattern: the four real counters land verbatim on `Turn.token_usage`, while the derived `totalInputTokens` and the capacity `maxInputTokens` are wire-preserved but never summed into spend.

## Verified against the goal ladder

- **L1**: an amp thread shared to Pathbase renders every beat with per-message token lines
- **L2** (`0.0.1785170481-ga5b614`): `path resume --harness amp` passes the probing question ("most-used tool?" answered `shell_command`, six times)
- **L3** (Claude Code 2.1.220): the amp-shared doc resumes in real `claude -r` and answers correctly
- **L4** (`0.0.1785228716-gedda19`): a real 138-step Claude Code session resumes in real amp and answers correctly

Try it: `path share --harness amp --anon`, then `path resume <url> --harness amp` (one billed turn) or `--harness claude`. `scripts/verify-amp-live.sh` reruns the loop in an isolated home.

## Quality gates

- Two adversarial review rounds, all findings fixed test-first. Round-two highlights: counter-free usage stubs preserve `model`/`timestamp` on the claude-to-amp leg, `CliWriter` feeds stdin from a dedicated thread (deadlock and EPIPE-masking fix), explicit-null cache counters round-trip via double-`Option` (they are `.nullable()` in Amp's zod schema), tolerant reads warn on malformed known-type blocks so schema drift cannot silently derive tool-less paths, and `last_activity` takes the max of all recency signals (the export's top-level `updatedAt` is frozen at creation time in the real capture).
- The cross-harness matrix has the amp row: every fixture through every projector. The cross-harness work surfaced two real gaps outside amp, both fixed here: the matrix caught cursor's projector losing file identity on patch-envelope sources (`toolpath-cursor` 0.2.1), and live resume verification caught claude-side resume needing a fresh UUIDv4 stem plus an unsigned-thinking strip (Claude Code 2.1.220 rejects replayed unsigned thinking with a 400).
- Tests: `toolpath-amp` 126 unit + 8 integration + 2 doc over a real captured fixture (byte-identical copies in-crate and at `test-fixtures/amp/`), and `path-cli` 364 unit + 127 integration. Workspace build / test / `clippy -D warnings` / fmt all green.
- Rebased onto current `main` (`fe308b3`) including integration with the new cache-sync manifest: amp joins git as a never-discovered type (server-side, nothing to stat-fingerprint), so `p import amp` / `share` remain the ingestion paths. One note for reviewers: because the rebase put the sync manifest underneath the whole branch, mid-branch commits do not build individually (the tip is green, and a first-parent bisect on main is unaffected).

## Docs

Format reference at `docs/agents/formats/amp/` (9 files, every claim version-stamped, since Amp builds churn fast and each thread pins its creating build via `env.initial.platform.clientVersion`). Release checklist items 1-11 landed (crates.json, release.sh tiers, CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, crate README). Build provenance (plan, review, build log, piece prompts) ships at `docs/roger-amp-plan/`, and the `amp-m0`..`amp-m6` milestone tags on the fork mark each piece's DoD commit.

## Known limitations (preview)

Listing costs one `export` per thread (Amp exposes no cheap metadata surface, accepted). Resume into amp costs one billed turn and transfers context, not native tool blocks, stated in the CLI output and help. Sub-agent (`Task`) results are bare strings with no child thread, so delegated turns stay empty, matching Claude/Copilot. No git state exists in threads, so `base.vcs_*` is always `None`.
